Detecting the number of supported touches for a particular device used
to be tricky
column2: both because early forms of the driver didn't have a very

column1: good HID parser and because early hardware didn't always advertise the
actual number. At the time
column2: we added a block of code which would ensure

column1: that touch_max would always be equal to at least 1 on any touch device
and relied on setting touch_max to e.g. 2 only for the multitouch-capable
exceptions.
The common case has since flipped
column2: and the driver and descriptors can

column1: reliably detect the number of touches supported by modern sensors.
Because of this
column2: it makes sense to remove the fixup code and instead

column1: place static declarations of ""touch_max = 1"" for these old devices. It
isn't entirely clear if all 2-finger devices actually report a maximum
number of touches so we leave these declarations still in place.
For the eagle-eyed
column2: the ""> BAMBOO_PT"" condition was originally equivalent

column1: to "">= TABLETPC""
column2: which is what the intent was. This commit doesn't have

column1: to consider the types introduced in the interim since they shouldn't be
affected
